scope: Terms of candidate sources for a public website run by a commercial roofing company that publishes derived per-tile files (streets, building shapes, addresses, past weather). Quotes are verbatim from live reads. Readings are not legal advice.
method: Live requests with curl through the configured proxy and CA bundle; redirects followed; HTTP status, bytes, SHA-256, server Date and read time (UTC) recorded per URL in the manifest.
Each quote was matched against the downloaded text after whitespace and quote-mark normalisation only (see verification).
Zip members (TIGER/Line, MSL structures and transportation) were read by range request: the last 64 KB for the central directory, then only the metadata member; CRC checked.
Web search was used only to find candidate URLs; no search-result text is quoted.
AGENTS.md rules 5, 6 and 9 read from the repository file and quoted verbatim.
No 403 or CDN block was worked around; blocked pages are listed as not read.
Downloads kept under 100 MB; the downloads folder is deleted after this record was written.
constraints_followed: Rule 7: live request and content check per source
No vendor or model names in this record

sources.name: Montana Code Annotated 2-6-1017 (in force) and 2-6-109 (repealed)

quotes.label: mca_1017_lead
quotes.quote: (1) Except as provided in subsections (3) through (10), to protect the privacy of those who deal with state and local government:

quotes.label: mca_1017_a
quotes.quote: (a) a public agency may not distribute or sell a distribution list without first securing the permission of those on the list; and

quotes.label: mca_1017_b
quotes.quote: (b) a list of persons prepared by a public agency may not be used as a distribution list except by the public agency or another public agency without first securing the permission of those on the list.

quotes.label: mca_1017_2
quotes.quote: (2) As used in this section, "distribution list" means any list of personal contact information collected by a public agency and used to facilitate unsolicited contact with individuals on the distribution list.

quotes.label: mca_1017_3
quotes.quote: (3) This section does not prevent an individual from compiling a distribution list by examination of records that are otherwise open to public inspection.

quotes.label: mca_1017_4
quotes.quote: (4) This section does not apply to the lists of:

quotes.label: mca_1017_11
quotes.quote: (11) A person violating the provisions of subsection (1)(b) is guilty of a misdemeanor.

quotes.label: mca_1017_hist
quotes.quote: History: En. Sec. 11, Ch. 348, L. 2015; amd. Sec. 1, Ch. 51, L. 2019; amd. Sec. 1, Ch. 147, L. 2019; amd. Sec. 1, Ch. 457, L. 2021.

reading.status_2_6_1017: In force on the live page (Montana Code Annotated 2025); history through 2021.
reading.status_2_6_109: Repealed on the live page: "2-6-109. Repealed. Sec. 59, Ch. 348, L. 2015."
reading.note: Both history lines cite the same 2015 session law (Ch. 348, L. 2015); the 2-6-1017 history begins there. The relationship is for counsel to confirm.
reading.plain_reading_not_legal_advice: Subsection (1) restricts two things: (a) a public agency giving out or selling a distribution list without the permission of the people on it, and (b) anyone other than the agency using a list of persons prepared by a public agency as a distribution list without that permission. Breaching (1)(b) is a misdemeanor under (11). Subsection (2) defines a distribution list by content and purpose: personal contact information collected by a public agency and used to facilitate unsolicited contact with individuals on the list. The definition does not mention names. For a site that shows addresses without names, the text leaves three open points: whether an address point is personal contact information; whether a public, searchable map of address points is a list of persons prepared by a public agency; and whether the site facilitates unsolicited contact when the operator is a roofing business that may use the map for outreach. A map with no names, no export and no contact function is a different case from a list handed to a sales team, but the text does not decide it. Subsection (3) allows compiling a list from records otherwise open to public inspection, which may be relevant to how the address data is obtained, not to what the site does with it. The exceptions in (4) to (10) name specific groups (registered electors, licence holders, property owners in a water or sewer district, sign-in sheets and others); none of the listed exceptions is an address-point dataset on the text read.
reading.msl_reference: The MSL parcel metadata cites 2-6-1017 and 2-6-109 for owner-bearing parcel data. The structures and transportation metadata do not cite either section (see mca_refs in the sources).
reading.b3_brief_note: The B3 brief (lines 36 and 162) plans to say that 2-6-1017 and 2-6-109 concern lists of persons. Because 2-6-109 is repealed on the live page, the About text should cite 2-6-1017 only, or describe 2-6-109 as repealed, for counsel to decide.

counsel_must_read_before_go_live.why: The reading of 2-6-1017 for an address map used by a commercial business is a counsel question, and the repealed 2-6-109 must not be cited as current law.

agents_md_rules.rule_5_verbatim: 5. **Evidence honesty.** Keep forecast, radar estimate, point report, official alert and inspection separate. Never state confirmed damage, insurance eligibility or a damage probability. No report is not "no hail." Missing inputs show "Data unavailable," never an all-clear. Demo data only under the demo event, labelled DEMO everywhere.
agents_md_rules.rule_6_verbatim: 6. **Official alerts.** Match by warning polygon, else the place's NWS forecast zone / county / fire-zone codes. Null geometry never means "no alert"; can't-tell shows as can't-tell. Never clear a warning after a failed request. No AI-generated text anywhere in the alert path.
agents_md_rules.rule_9_verbatim: 9. **No "best" claims** for any provider or model until the evaluation in `docs/ROADMAP.md` supports it.
words_must_respect: No statement of confirmed damage, insurance eligibility or a damage probability in the About, terms or layer text (rule 5).
No report is not "no hail": terms and data-gap sentences must say that a missing record does not mean that nothing happened (rule 5; the SWDI disclaimer supports this wording).
A failed or blocked source shows "Data unavailable", never an all-clear (rule 5); a licence that cannot be confirmed should disable the layer, not leave it silently on.
Official alert text is never AI-generated and the terms text is not alert text; the About text must not claim alert coverage (rule 6).
Null geometry never means no alert (rule 6); the same caution applies to building or address gaps, which must not be described as absence of buildings.
No "best" claims (rule 9): NCEI wording such as "best available information" must not be repeated as a site claim.
Plain wording, sentence case, no em-dashes in site text (conventions and owner preferences).

counsel_questions: MCA 2-6-1017: is a public map of address points with no names a "list of persons prepared by a public agency" or "personal contact information" under subsections (1)(b) and (2)?
